name: genotype-00-build-integrity
title: Does a ParCa-level knockout reconstruct into a self-consistent sim_data?

canonical_runs.name: wt-fast
canonical_runs.label: WT arm - fast-mode ParCa, all 9 steps, default bundle

canonical_runs.name: ko-fast
canonical_runs.label: lacY KO arm - fast-mode ParCa on the generated variant bundle

question: When a gene is deleted from the chromosome and the ParCa is rebuilt on the perturbed genome, does the resulting sim_data stay self-consistent? Concretely: is every retained feature's sequence exactly what it should be, does the feature inventory change by exactly the expected amount, does every coordinate still lie inside the shortened chromosome, and does the fit converge with its parameters in range - before any physiological reading is attempted.

assumptions.text: A ParCa build is deterministic given its inputs, so the same genotype bundle reconstructs to the same sim_data. This is what lets a manifest hash serve as the genotype identity and lets builds be cached rather than repeated.

★ The round-trip invariant must be TWO-BRANCH, and the obvious one-branch form is vacuous for the defect it most needs to catch. "Every retained feature's sequence is unchanged" is wrong twice: features straddling the deletion are SUPPOSED to lose those bases, and once that is relaxed the check still cannot see an off-by-one splice, because an off-by-one preserves every length. The working form asserts byte-identity only for features whose length is unchanged, and for shrunk features asserts the sequence equals the original with exactly the deleted span excised.

Coordinates in the EcoCyc-derived flat files are 1-based INCLUSIVE - a feature spanning [L, R] occupies genome_sequence[L-1:R]. Verified two ways: getter_functions.py:194 slices exactly that way, and of 174 '+'-strand genes 157 start with ATG under that reading versus 0 under the 0-based one. Load-bearing, because feature LENGTHS stay correct under an off-by-one while the sequence silently shifts.

A knockout that fails to build is a RESULT, not a failed study. For an essential gene the ParCa fit may not converge at all, which is a legitimate and informative outcome qualitatively unlike the translation-level knockout's. The tests below are written so that a non-converging fit is recorded rather than treated as infrastructure failure.

variants.name: single-gene-knockout
variants.perturbation: ParCa-level knockout - the gene is spliced out of the chromosome before reconstruction, so downstream coordinates shift and the fit sees a genome without it.
variants.expected_contrast: The chromosome is shorter by exactly the gene's length; the gene is absent from sim_data rather than present at zero abundance; features straddling the deletion are truncated; every other feature's sequence is untouched. Physiology is deliberately NOT read here.

model_settings.name: target-gene
model_settings.detail:
SATISFIED - first target is EG10526 (lacY), and it builds: a fast-mode ParCa on the lacY knockout bundle completed all 9 steps in 104 s, exit 0, with mechanistic_fit_status ok for supply, export and uptake (2026-08-13, main @ 60f3e4b8). The 7-8 dangling references the generator leaves by design (D17) did not break the build.
Rationale for the choice, unchanged: EG10526 is the gene the landed translation-level study (ko-and-media) already uses, so the two knockout mechanisms share a reference point, and it sits inside the lac operon, which exercises the straddling-feature branch of the round-trip invariant. On the real KB a lacY deletion truncates one transcription unit and shortens four others. A non-operonic gene would leave the second branch of the invariant untested.

model_settings.name: effective-build-from-the-declared-manifest
model_settings.detail:
SATISFIED by v2ecoli#482, verified 2026-08-13 on main @ 60f3e4b8. Declaring a genotype is not the same as building from it, and until #482 it was not: step_01_initialize.py warned "the fit will proceed against the injected raw_data; the declared manifest is provenance only", so a run would have built the wild type and merely noted a mismatch.
#482 added _resolve_raw_data(): when no KnowledgeBaseEcoli is injected it builds one, honouring the declared bundle_manifest via SourceBundle(base_manifest=...). The chain is parca generator param -> _build_step_slots -> step_01_initialize.py -> SourceBundle. The v2ecoli-parca CLI honours the same manifest. The residual warning now fires only when an INJECTED raw_data disagrees with the declaration, which is a mismatch alarm rather than a statement that declaration is inert.
Verified against a real lacY (EG10526) knockout bundle: genome spliced by exactly 1254 bp (the 361926-363179 span), the gene tombstoned with null coordinates, all downstream features shifted by exactly 1254.
Something must construct raw_data FROM the declared manifest when a study runs. Verified 2026-08-07 that v2ecoli#468 did NOT close this - that PR fixed override precedence inside SourceBundle (a variant's generated key now wins over parca_overrides) and touched only sources.py plus its tests. Both are needed and neither substitutes for the other: #468 makes a variant's files survive once you build from them; this gate is about building from them at all.
Recorded as its own gate because a reader scanning this list would otherwise conclude the KO generator is the last blocker on the build path, and it is not.

model_settings.name: ko-generator
model_settings.detail:
SATISFIED. The ecoli-sources KO generator that emits the perturbed bundle + manifest landed as ecoli-sources#12 and is reachable from v2ecoli: the pin in pyproject.toml moved to rev 2dfabd52 in v2ecoli#471. Merging in ecoli-sources does not make code reachable from v2ecoli until the pin moves, so both halves were required.
This study was its acceptance target, and the generator passes it: knockout() writes the six coupled canonical keys and compose_variant_bundle() produces a manifest that ParCa builds from (see the effective-build gate above).

perturbed-genome-reconstructs-without-co.detail: genotype_build_integrity card grades within_tol on the identical content-addressed bundle (genotype_id 2e013536817c75d2): two-branch round trip over genes, transcription units and DNA sites reports 0 differing features, with the shrunk branch non-vacuously exercised by the lac-operon TUs. Discrimination proven by fault injection (tests/test_genotype_build_card.py, 14/14): a 1 bp length-preserving corruption and an off-by-one span both fail this check while the length axis passes.

chromosome-length-changes-by-exactly-the.detail: Delta is exactly 1254 bp (span 361926-363179): 4641652 -> 4640398. Card axis chromosome_length passes.

all-coordinates-stay-within-the-shortene.detail: coordinate_bounds axis: 0 violations across genes, transcription units and DNA sites (1 <= left <= right <= genome_length).

deleted-gene-is-functionally-absent-from.detail: EG10526's row survives in `genes` with coordinates nulled (the tombstone), and the gene is excluded from both valid_gene_ids and all_mRNA_cistrons - functional absence, not id absence (D16). Card axes tombstone + functional_absence pass; the no-op control (WT graded against itself) fails both, so a pass is discriminating.

parca-fit-completes-and-fitted-parameter.detail: The fit COMPLETES on the perturbed genome: all 9 steps exit 0, mechanistic_fit_status {supply: ok, export: ok, uptake: ok} (out/genotype-00/ko/parca_state.pkl). Parameter-RANGE grading is deliberately not performed: this is a fast-regime build (7 of 51 cell_specs) and the study's run-mode limitation forbids grading fast-mode fitted parameters. PARTIAL, not PASS, until a full-mode build exists - recorded honestly rather than upgraded.

findings.statement: A ParCa-level lacY knockout builds end to end through the supplier-side generator path - bundle generation (<1 s, content-addressed), all 9 ParCa steps (78 s fast regime), mechanistic fits ok - and the reconstructed knowledge base passes every structural integrity axis: two-branch sequence round trip (0 corrupted features across genes, TUs and DNA sites), exact 1254 bp chromosome shortening, all coordinates in bounds, and functional absence of the deleted gene via the tombstone mechanism.

evidence.observed: Card verdict within_tol (5/5 graded structural axes); WT and KO arms built 2026-08-14, runtimes.json 78 s each.

findings.next_action: Grade the two ParCa-fit axes against a full-mode build when one is warranted; until then they stay ungraded/PARTIAL by design. The descriptive studies (01-06) now have a working build path to run against.

tests.name: perturbed-genome-reconstructs-without-coordinate-or-sequence-corruption
tests.question: After the deletion, is every retained coordinate-bearing feature's sequence exactly what it should be?

measure.detail: Two-branch round-trip over all coordinate-bearing features (genes, transcription units, DNA sites; ~12.8k on the real KB). Unchanged length ⇒ sequence must be byte-identical to the wild-type read. Shrunk ⇒ sequence must equal the wild-type read with exactly the deleted span excised. Report the count in each branch as well as the corruption count, so a pass cannot be vacuous - zero shrunk features means the second branch was never exercised and the target gene was a poor choice.

tests.name: chromosome-length-changes-by-exactly-the-deleted-span
tests.question: Does the genome shorten by exactly the gene's length, no more and no less?

measure.detail: len(wild_type.genome_sequence) - len(knockout.genome_sequence), against right_end_pos - left_end_pos + 1 for the target gene. Note this check is NOT sufficient on its own: an off-by-one splice preserves length exactly, which is why the round-trip test above is the primary and this is supporting.

tests.name: all-coordinates-stay-within-the-shortened-chromosome
tests.question: Does every surviving feature satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= genome_length after the shift?

measure.detail: Count features violating the bound, across genes, transcription units and DNA sites. Catches a shift applied in the wrong direction or to the wrong side of the cut.

tests.name: deleted-gene-is-functionally-absent-from-sim_data
tests.question: Is the gene excluded from the transcribed and translated sets, rather than still being expressed at some level?

measure.detail:
Membership of the deleted gene in the two sets the knowledge base uses to mean "on the chromosome": valid_gene_ids (getter_functions.py, genes with positions that are not pseudogenes/phantom genes) and all_mRNA_cistrons (translation.py). Expect exclusion from both.
★ NOT id-absence. The knockout TOMBSTONES the deleted gene - it nulls the coordinates and keeps the row - so the gene id legitimately persists in `genes` and in sim_data.process.replication.gene_data. An axis asserting the id appears nowhere would FAIL ON CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, which is the mirror image of a vacuous test and just as useless.
The tombstone is the KB's existing vocabulary for "not on the chromosome" - 21 of 4,747 shipped genes are permanently in that state - and both sets above already filter on exactly that null-coordinate check. Removing the row instead would leave a dangling cistron, since the deletion does not touch rnas/proteins.
Functional absence is also the claim that actually distinguishes this from a translation-level knockout, which leaves the gene transcribed and consuming RNAP capacity. So this axis now tests the mechanism rather than a proxy for it.

tests.name: parca-fit-completes-and-fitted-parameters-stay-in-range
tests.question: Does the fit converge on the perturbed genome, and do its fitted parameters - the mechanistic amino-acid supply kcats in particular - stay in a plausible range?

measure.detail:
Condition count fitted, cache-bundle artifact presence, and the fitted AA-supply kcats against their wild-type values. RFC-007 flags ParCa-level changes as interacting with mechanistic amino-acid supply parameter fitting, and Riley identified this as the specific un-stress-tested area; genotype-03 probes it with AA-pathway genes, and this axis is the general build-time detector. A non-converging fit is RECORDED as the outcome, not treated as a broken study - for an essential gene it may be the correct answer.
Count fitted conditions as len(cell_specs), NOT len(conditions). Measured 2026-08-13 on main @ 60f3e4b8: a fast-mode build has conditions = 51 but cell_specs = 7 (basal, with_aa, acetate, succinate, no_oxygen, and the two CPLX-125 arms). `conditions` is the full condition LIST and reads 51 in both modes, so an axis implemented against it would pass at 51 on a fast build and never discriminate. cell_specs holds the conditions actually fitted, which is the quantity this axis means.
Mode is therefore load-bearing and must be recorded with any result from this axis. See the run-mode limitation below.

readouts.name: feature-sequence-round-trip
readouts.description: Per-feature comparison of wild-type vs knockout sequence at the feature's own coordinates, bucketed by unchanged-length / shrunk / removed.

readouts.name: chromosome-length
readouts.description: Genome length before and after the deletion.

readouts.name: feature-inventory
readouts.description:
Counts of genes, transcription units and DNA sites before and after.
DNA sites are counted EXCLUDING ids matching `G0-DNAA-*`. Those 13 rows (oriC and dnaA-promoter DnaA boxes) are supplied by v2ecoli's `flat_overrides/dna_sites.tsv`, not by the ecoli-sources base table. A knockout variant generates the `dna_sites` key, and a generated key takes precedence over the whole-file override (v2ecoli#466/#468), so the 13 rows are absent from every knockout build. The count therefore falls by 13 regardless of which gene is deleted - measured identical for lacY (EG10526), pgi (EG10702) and tpiA (EG11015) - which makes it a constant property of the build path, not an effect of the perturbation. Including them would attribute a fixed -13 offset to the knockout.
The exclusion keeps this readout measuring what it claims to measure. It does not address the absence itself, which is tracked separately and is out of scope for this study.

readouts.name: deleted-gene-set-membership
readouts.description: Whether the deleted gene appears in valid_gene_ids and in all_mRNA_cistrons, plus the tombstone's own state (row present, coordinates null). Reported together so a pass is legible: the id SHOULD still be found in `genes`, and SHOULD NOT be found in either functional set.

readouts.name: fitted-aa-supply-kcats
readouts.description: Mechanistic amino-acid supply kcats from the fitted sim_data, knockout vs wild type. The only readout here still requiring a ParCa run, and the reason the two fit axes report `ungraded`: a fast-mode build's fitted parameters must not be graded (see the run-mode limitation). Needs a full-mode build to become gradeable.

model_change: None to the simulation. The change under test is upstream of it: the knowledge base is reconstructed from a perturbed genome. The chromosome-deletion path this study exercises lands in v2ecoli#455.

implementation_requirements.name: genotype declaration on the build surface
implementation_requirements.detail: A way for a study to name the genotype it builds - a bundle manifest hash or an equivalent - reaching the parca composite. DONE in v2ecoli#457 (bundle_manifest / bundle_overrides on the parca generator, threaded to InitializeStep with a declared-vs-injected cross-check). Was the blocking item; no longer is.

implementation_requirements.name: ecoli-sources KO generator
implementation_requirements.detail: Emits the perturbed bundle + complete manifest for a chromosome-level knockout. This study is its acceptance target.

implementation_requirements.name: build-integrity report card
implementation_requirements.detail: Gen-2 ReportCardStep rendering the axes above, so the verdict is a card rather than a one-off script. Reusable by every genotype study downstream.

implementation_requirements.name: wild-type reference build
implementation_requirements.detail: The unperturbed sim_data every comparison above is taken against. Available from the existing full-ParCa path.

alternative_hypotheses: A corrupted build could come from the generator rather than the deletion transform - a malformed bundle or a manifest pointing at the wrong files. Distinguished by running the same invariant directly on the knowledge base, without the generator, which is what the unit tests in v2ecoli#455 do.

A fit that fails to converge may reflect the gene's essentiality rather than a broken build. Distinguished by the sequence and coordinate axes: those pass or fail independently of whether the fit converges.
falsifiability: Any corrupted feature, out-of-range coordinate, or unexpected length change fails this study outright. The invariants are exact rather than banded - there is no tolerance to argue about - which is why this study can be graded while the rest of the investigation stays descriptive.
limitations: Establishes that the build is internally consistent, NOT that the resulting physiology is sensible. Everything about how the cell behaves is downstream and belongs to studies 01-06.
A single-genotype build integrity check does not establish the transform is correct in general. Genome-wide confidence needs the panel, and ultimately the tranche-B runner.
The AA-kcat axis has no band yet, so it is a recorded observation rather than a graded criterion on the first pass.

Run mode is load-bearing and the two tiers answer different questions. A fast-mode build (~104 s measured) fits 7 of 51 conditions and is sufficient for the structural readouts - sequence round-trip, chromosome length, feature inventory, and deleted-gene set membership were all measured on one. A full-mode build (several hours, per docs/generate_full_parca.md) fits all conditions and is required before any claim about FITTED PARAMETER VALUES, because the CLI's own --allow-partial-fit help flags step 9's mechanistic fits as failing on "numerically-marginal kinetics (e.g. debug mode's truncated TF set)" - the exact regime a fast build is in. So fast-mode kcat magnitudes are not trustworthy and must not be graded.
The practical consequence is that this study can screen a genotype panel cheaply in fast mode and reserve full-mode builds for genotypes advancing to physiology. That is what makes a panel or a genome-wide screen tractable at all: the alternative prices every genotype at hours.
